inputs.root_cause: SAL-NRRD-OBL-2085AD256AFE6E96's own missing_behavior named a precise, structural gap: decode_encoding()'s trailing-payload rejection happens as a hard exception at load() time, before validate() -- which only ever accepted an already-loaded NrrdDocument/mapping -- could run on the offending source at all. Two prior ticks (FF6-EVENT-000288, and a fresh re-investigation this tick) confirmed this needs new plumbing, unlike the UBL-WRITE-001 case that reused an existing dict.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 3 new tests directly exercising the new validate()-accepts-raw-source path for trailing gzip data, trailing bzip2 data, and a clean-source regression guard; independently verified via a standalone repro before any test was written.
inputs.regression_tier: full nrrd suite plus 6-format regression, mypy --strict, ruff

execution_steps: 1. Re-investigated the deferred nrrd trailing-payload item first: confirmed decode_encoding() has no existing diagnostics-collection mechanism reaching validate() (NrrdDocument.recovery_actions exists on the model but is never populated by any caller -- genuinely dead infrastructure for a different, separately-tracked obligation, NRRD-LIFECYCLE-001's own 'recovery mode', not reusable here without conflating scope).

2. Read the obligation's own authority text (RF-NRRD-00003, kind: security_expectation, 'hostile headers must fail cheaply') to confirm the fix must NOT weaken the actual rejection -- only change how it is reported. Ruled out making decode_encoding tolerant of trailing compressed-stream garbage (would silently accept potentially hidden/appended data, the opposite of this session's own hidden-data-hunting discipline).

3. Found NRRD's validate() could not even accept raw bytes/paths: `validate(b'garbage')` raised an uncaught AttributeError, confirming validate() was strictly post-load. Compared directly against format_factory.ora.lifecycle.validate()'s own proven pattern (re-parse from raw source internally, catch format errors, wrap as a FATAL Diagnostic) -- a pattern this same session had just implemented and tested for ora moments earlier in this tick.

4. Extended validate()'s accepted type to NrrdDocument | Mapping | BinarySource; added an else-branch that calls load() internally and catches (NrrdError, ResourceLimitError), returning ValidationReport([Diagnostic('nrrd.source.unreadable', str(exc), severity=Severity.FATAL)]) instead of propagating.

5. Verified with a standalone repro: a raw NRRD source with trailing gzip garbage now returns a FATAL diagnostic via validate() (is_valid=False) instead of raising; a nonexistent path, a clean valid source (str path, Path, and raw bytes) all behave correctly.

6. Added 3 tests to the existing tests/python/nrrd/test_obligation_compressed_trailing_data.py (natural home, already covers this obligation's sibling load()-raises behavior): trailing-gzip diagnostic, trailing-bzip2 diagnostic, clean-source-still-succeeds regression guard.
7. Ran mypy --strict (clean), ruff (clean), the full nrrd suite (619 -> 622 passed, +3), and the 6-format regression (3637 -> 3640 passed, 0 failed).

8. Promoted SAL-NRRD-OBL-2085AD256AFE6E96 partial->implemented in the ledger, citing the new tests and appending an FF6-EVENT-000291-dated addendum to implemented_behavior rather than rewriting prior history; cleared missing_behavior. Reconciler confirmed 19/65 -> 18/65 unresolved.
